name: assembly-over-eskibeat
style: early-2000s eskibeat grime instrumental, 140 BPM, cold and half-empty; hollow square-wave bass in short clipped stabs, 8-bit ping-pong eski clicks on the off-beats, one dry clap on 2 and 4, a single frosty plinking synth stab looping, long silences between hits; vocals: a whole primary-school assembly, two hundred kids aged 7 to 11 in unison, flat bored London accents, dutiful and blase, plodding in slow hymn metre and ignoring the beat; big echoey school-hall reverb on the children only, beat bone-dry; stops dead on the last word
exclude: piano, organ, adult vocals, rap, pads, solo singer, strings
lyrics:
[Intro: eskibeat alone, one bar]

[Verse: whole school in unison, slow hymn time, bored, off the beat]
We can't afford a bed for you,
The purse is far too thin;
There is room on all those islands,
But you will sleep in a bin.

[End: beat cuts dead, no tail]
